0.0.n: Names the next step in the cooking process.

0.1.n: Marks 次 as the topic, introducing the next step.

0.2.n: 衣 refers to a food coating here, not clothing.

0.3.n: Marks 衣 as what is being applied.

0.4.n: Polite form of つける, describing the action the speaker will do next.

1.0.n: A borrowed food name written in katakana.

1.1.n: Links examples without suggesting they are the only ones.

1.2.n: Names a Japanese dish of ingredients fried in batter.

1.3.n: Shows that fried chicken and tempura are examples of a larger group.

1.4.n: Connects the example foods to their outer area, 周り.

1.6.n: Refers to the area surrounding the food.

1.7.n: Links 周り to 部分, specifying which part is meant.

1.8.n: Refers to the outer layer of the food.

1.9.n: Marks the part being given a name in the pattern AをBと言います.

1.11.n: This is the Japanese term being introduced for the food’s outer layer.

1.13.n: Marks 衣 as the quoted name used with 言います.

1.14.n: Polite form of 言う; AをBと言います means to call A B.

2.0.n: Describes the earlier time associated with this use of the word.

2.1.n: Connects 昔 to 言葉, describing language from earlier times.

2.2.n: Refers to older Japanese usage rather than one particular word.

2.3.n: Marks older language as the context in which 衣 has this meaning.

2.5.n: Gives the older meaning of 衣 using a common modern word.

2.7.n: Connects 服 to 意味, identifying the meaning being explained.

2.8.n: The word being explained, 衣, is left unstated because it is already understood.

2.9.n: Ends the explanation politely; the verb itself is not in the past tense.

0.tip: 衣をつける means to coat food; the food itself is left unstated here.

1.lit: Fried chicken, tempura, and so on: their outside part we call coating.
1.tip: The pattern AをBと言います introduces a name: A is called B.

2.lit: In language of long ago, it is the meaning of clothing.
2.tip: 昔の言葉で sets an older-language context, even though です is not past tense.
